deck_name: Industrial Automation: PLCs, IEC 61131-3, Modbus & OPC UA

cards.prompt: What are the four sequential stages of a deterministic PLC Scan Cycle?
cards.answer: 1. Read Physical Inputs -> 2. Execute Program Logic -> 3. Write Physical Outputs -> 4. Housekeeping / Communications
accepted_answers: Input scan, Program execution, Output scan, Housekeeping
cards.explanation: Snapshotting inputs into an input image table at the start of the scan ensures input values remain consistent throughout the entire logic evaluation pass.

cards.prompt: Name the five programming languages standardized under IEC 61131-3 for Programmable Logic Controllers.
cards.answer: Ladder Diagram (LD), Function Block Diagram (FBD), Structured Text (ST), Instruction List (IL), and Sequential Function Chart (SFC)
cards.explanation: Structured Text (ST) resembles Pascal/C and is preferred for complex math/state machines, while LD/FBD excel at discrete Boolean interlocks.

cards.prompt: In IEC 61131-3, what is the difference between a Function (`FC`) and a Function Block (`FB`)?
cards.answer: A Function (`FC`) is stateless and returns the same output for given inputs; a Function Block (`FB`) retains internal persistent state across scan cycles
accepted_answers: FC is stateless FB has persistent internal state
cards.explanation: Timers (`TON`), counters (`CTU`), and PID controllers must be Function Blocks because they store elapsed time or integral accumulators between scans.

cards.prompt: Why are industrial Emergency Stop (E-Stop) buttons wired as Normally Closed (NC) contacts?
cards.answer: Fail-safe detection: if a wire breaks, vibrates loose, or loses power, the circuit opens and immediately trips the machine into a safe stop
cards.explanation: A Normally Open (NO) E-stop would silently fail to stop a hazardous machine if a conductor severed.

cards.prompt: Why do industrial analog sensors commonly use a 4–20 mA current loop instead of a 0–10 V voltage signal?
cards.answer: Current is immune to resistive voltage drop over long cables, and a 0 mA reading distinguishes a broken wire ('live zero') from a valid 0% reading (4 mA)
accepted_answers: immune to voltage drop and 4mA live zero detects broken wires
cards.explanation: Over hundreds of feet of factory conduit, voltage signals attenuate and pick up EMI, whereas current stays constant everywhere in a series loop.

cards.prompt: What physical layer does Modbus RTU typically run over, and how does it frame messages without start/stop delimiter bytes?
cards.answer: RS-485 differential serial, using a silent bus interval of at least 3.5 character times to mark frame boundaries
cards.explanation: Because Modbus RTU transmits raw binary bytes, any gap longer than 3.5 character times resets the receiver state machine for a new frame.

cards.prompt: In Modbus, what is the difference between Coils (0x) and Holding Registers (4x)?
cards.answer: Coils are 1-bit read/write discrete outputs; Holding Registers are 16-bit read/write analog/configuration words
cards.explanation: Discrete Inputs (1x) are 1-bit read-only, and Input Registers (3x) are 16-bit read-only.

cards.prompt: How does OPC UA improve upon legacy OPC Classic (DCOM) for smart manufacturing and CPS?
cards.answer: OPC UA is platform-independent (runs on Linux/RTOS/Windows), uses firewall-friendly TCP/HTTPS ports, supports rich semantic Information Models, and includes built-in X.509 mTLS encryption
accepted_answers: cross-platform, built-in security, rich information modeling
cards.explanation: Legacy OPC Classic relied on Windows-only Microsoft DCOM, which was notoriously difficult to route through firewalls and lacked modern cryptography.

cards.prompt: In OPC UA (`open62541`), what is the difference between Polling (`Read` service) and `MonitoredItems` inside a `Subscription`?
cards.answer: Polling repeatedly queries values on a timer; Subscriptions push data change notifications from server to client only when a value changes beyond a deadband
accepted_answers: Subscriptions push changes on deadband instead of constant polling
cards.explanation: Subscriptions drastically reduce network bandwidth while preserving deterministic publish intervals and sequence numbers.

cards.prompt: An IEC 61131-3 `TON` (On-Delay Timer) has `PT := T#500ms`. `IN` turns TRUE at t = 0 ms, stays TRUE until t = 300 ms, then turns FALSE. What is `Q` at t = 300 ms and t = 600 ms?
cards.code:
Timer1(IN := SensorActive, PT := T#500ms);
MotorCmd := Timer1.Q;
cards.answer: FALSE at 300 ms and FALSE at 600 ms
cards.explanation: A `TON` timer only sets `Q := TRUE` if `IN` remains continuously TRUE for the full preset time (`500 ms`). Dropping `IN` at 300 ms immediately resets `ET` to 0.

cards.prompt: Why does Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) or EtherCAT outperform standard TCP/IP Ethernet for multi-axis motion control?
cards.answer: Standard Ethernet is non-deterministic under congestion, whereas EtherCAT/TSN guarantee bounded sub-millisecond cycle times and nanosecond clock synchronization (IEEE 1588 PTP)
accepted_answers: deterministic bounded latency and IEEE 1588 clock synchronization
cards.explanation: EtherCAT processes frames 'on the fly' in hardware at each slave node without store-and-forward switch delays.

cards.prompt: What do SIL (IEC 61508) and PL (ISO 13849) measure in industrial control systems?
cards.answer: Safety Integrity Level (SIL 1–4) and Performance Level (PL a–e) quantify the reliability and probability of dangerous failure per hour for safety-related control functions
accepted_answers: Safety Integrity Level and Performance Level
cards.explanation: High-risk robotic cells typically require SIL 3 / PL e using redundant dual-channel safety relays or safety PLCs with cross-monitoring.
